THE HIGH-VALUE QUESTION THIS RESOLVES: actual_duration's declared 'set on close' semantics is now falsified in both directions on the same field, on two sessions closed back to back. 780 (null before, null after) shows close does not populate a previously-unset value. 779 (210 before, 210 after) shows close does not even touch an already-set value — it is neither recomputed nor overwritten. Combined with this capability's own guidance text ('the handler's actual_duration pass-through is commented out, so posting a duration here returns 200 and changes nothing'), the mechanism is now clear: actual_duration is set ONLY as a side effect elsewhere (apparently when a log is created directly on a session, consistent with 779 = 120+90 = sum of its own two logged elapsed_time values), never by this close call despite its declared description, and never recomputed for a clone whose logs arrived via copy rather than direct creation (780's clone-copied logs still carry elapsed_time 45/120 in `timeline`, yet never contributed to `actual_duration`). The declared 'set on close' text for this field is confirmed wrong, not merely stale.

THE OTHER HIGH-VALUE QUESTION -- DOES CLOSING LOCK THE SESSION: yes. A follow-up update_exploratory_session on closed session 780 (title-only change, otherwise harmless) was rejected with HTTP 400, body {success:false, message:'The API request is invalid or improperly formed'}. This is an HONEST 4xx rejection, not a silent no-op under 200 -- the lock is real and is surfaced as a real error, unlike the family's other confirmed silent-no-op defects (update_filter's inert entity field, unlink_test_runs_from_test_plan's 200-with-no-effect). The error body itself does not match this family's declared 400 error envelope ({success:false, error:{code,message,details}}) -- it is the flat {success:false, message} shape -- but that specific mismatch is already documented verbatim in update_exploratory_session's own guidance ('Upstream validation failures all arrive as 400 {success:false, message:...}'), so it is not a new finding here, just a re-confirmation. Per instruction, no error-vs-success schema diff is drawn from this 400 body.
